text:
maria: Uploaded a combined nsys + perfetto trace from the late-night load test. noticed a sharp HBM bandwidth jump when seqlen > ~4k, plus repeated KV cache evictions. attaching notes and trace links.

perf-bot: nsys run finished: /artifacts/nsys/1851234567_run01.qdstrace (2.1GB) - perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (expires in 7d) :white_check_mark:

jing: skimmed the trace - kernel timeline shows selector flipping from `fused_attention` -> `generic_gemm` around the same time HBM climbs. kernel launch rate increases which coincides w/ KV page churn. looks like batching heuristic is creating many small microbatches at high seqlen.

ryan: quick question — are we sure the selector is using seq_len and not token_count? I remember a change last quarter that introduced padding-aware token_count for routing. that could push borderline requests into the generic path.

maria: good call. i grepped the selector:

```c++
// runtime/kernel_selector.cpp
if (seq_len > 2000 || batch_tokens > 1000000) {
  return Kernel::GENERIC_GEMM; // safer fallback
} else {
  return Kernel::FUSED_ATTENTION;
}
```

This is from the shipping binary (v1.14). Notice `seq_len` threshold is 2000 here — our trace shows many requests with padded seq_len around 4096 even though effective tokens < 2k because of left-padding for chat history.

shawn: Aha. So two effects: (1) padded seq_len trips selector -> slower kernel, (2) slower kernel increases per-request latency -> microbatcher reduces aggregation window -> more KV reads per token -> THRASH. I ran a quick local diff replacing `seq_len` check with `effective_tokens()` and got much better behavior in a smoke run.

jing: do you have numbers?

shawn: smoke run (single A100):
- before: avg HBM 88% during 4k-profile window, tail p99 latency 620ms
- after (effective_tokens): avg HBM 52%, p99 420ms, observed fewer KV evictions in perfetto slices

maria: can you paste the patch?

shawn:
```diff
- if (seq_len > 2000 || batch_tokens > 1000000) {
+ if (effective_tokens > 2000 || batch_tokens > 1000000) {
    return Kernel::GENERIC_GEMM;
}
```

jing: that looks safe but we should add a guard for padded left context vs content length. also, the microbatcher has a `max_wait_ms` of 5ms in dedicated; maybe adaptive_wait that increases with seq_len would allow better batching for long sequences.

ryan: i sketched an adaptive heuristic:
```text
adaptive_wait_ms = clamp(base_wait + (seq_len / 1000) * scale, base_wait, max_wait)
```
Try base_wait=2ms, scale=3ms, max_wait=20ms. That bumped aggregation without hurting short seq RPCs in my synthetic runs.

maria: logging plan: 1) land selector change behind feature flag 2) add telemetry for selector_decision + effective_tokens histogram 3) experiment with adaptive microbatch wait in canary.

jing: for the perf traces, i also exported the mempipe HBM counters - nvprof shows sustained 300GB/s peaks when the generic kernel runs. fused path peaks at ~110GB/s. that's consistent with extra memory traffic from KV re-reads.

maria: summary action items:
- @shawn open PR for selector -> feature-flagged (include unit tests for padded vs effective lengths)
- @jing add perfetto slice with KV page refs annotated and upload to the canary dashboard
- @ryan prototype adaptive_wait and hook into canary config
- ops: roll canary to 5% after selector flag on (monitor HBM, KV_evictions, p99 latency)

ryan: noted. i can own the rollout config. I'll add alert thresholds: HBM > 75% sustained for 30s, KV_evictions rate spike > 200%

perf-bot: note: traced run also captured kernel stall metrics (SM __ldg throughput) - attaching csv: /artifacts/kernel_metrics/1851234567_kernel_metrics.csv

maria: thanks — let's keep replies short and update the PR links here. if the canary improves HBM and p99 we'll ship the selector change quickly. :rocket:

jing: one last note: add a regression test that runs a short perf suite with padded-left sequences to avoid reintroducing this.

maria: agree. adding test to the perf CI matrix.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from ryan, :eyes: from shawn)
